reason: The cited evidence shows that specific bulk HEAs and films can form protective oxide layers (E1, E3) and that oxide layers can lubricate under high loads (E8), but no evidence directly supports that applying an HEA coating to an HEA component forms a lubricating oxide layer that outperforms the uncoated HEA across the full stated range of conditions.
premises: HEA coatings form a stable, low-friction oxide layer that acts as a lubricant
This oxide layer prevents metal-to-metal contact, reducing friction and wear
The oxide layer remains effective across a wide temperature range (RT to 800°C)
The coating reduces COF and wear rate compared to uncoated HEA under high loads (1-9N) and sliding speeds (0.1-1 m/s)
